title: Granuloma architecture
dek: Macrophage core, lymphocytic cuff, often caseum. A structured lesion with gradients of oxygen, lipid, and drug — not a solid ball of latency.
story: The tuberculous granuloma is a spatially organised lesion: infected and uninfected macrophages (including epithelioid and foamy cells), a cuff of CD4/CD8 T cells and B-cell follicles in some human lesions, fibroblasts, and often a necrotic caseous core. It is a living tissue programme, not a prison that either succeeds or fails in binary.

Caseum is hypoxic, acidic, and full of host lipids. Bacilli there are slowly replicating or non-replicating, with altered drug susceptibility. Pyrazinamide’s clinical sterilizing role and rifamycin persistence both have lesion-pharmacology explanations. Isoniazid looks brilliant on log-phase broth and ordinary in caseum.

Cavitation is a granuloma that has emptied into an airway. High smear, high mutation supply, high transmission. HIV and anti-TNF dissolve the architecture toward poorly formed, multibacillary, disseminated disease — a pathogenesis fact with a diagnostic smear-negative pattern.
deep: C3HeB/FeJ “Kramnik” mice, rabbits, and macaques caseate; many C57BL/6 models do not. Fitting a four-month human regimen to a non-necrotic mouse CFU curve is a category error.
Lesion-centric PK (rifampin penetration into caseum is limited relative to vascularized cuff) is why sterilizing drugs are not interchangeable with cidal drugs.
Within-host diversity: different lesions in one lung can host different resistance minorities. A single sputum WGS is a sample of what drained today.
Calcified Ghon complexes are the radiology of old negotiation, not proof of sterility.

visual.caption: Idealised section of a necrotic granuloma. Oxygen and drug fall toward caseum; lymphocytes live in the cuff. Cavitation is this core opening to a bronchus.
visual.annotation: PZA and rifamycins earn their keep toward the core; INH earns it in replicating rims.

example.title: Smear 3+ from a cavity, IGRA positive in the spouse
example.setup: Index: cavitary smear 3+. Spouse: IGRA+, normal CXR, asymptomatic.

steps.title: Anatomy explains both
steps.body: The cavity is a transmission engine. The spouse has an immune memory assay after exposure, not proven disease.

steps.title: Different pharmacologic objects
steps.body: Index needs a sterilizing combination. Spouse, after disease exclusion, is a TPT candidate.

steps.title: Mutation supply
steps.body: The 3+ cavity is where monotherapy would fail in public. Do not “start INH while awaiting Xpert” in the index.

example.takeaway: Cuff versus caseum versus cavity are different drug problems.

choices: A sterile calcium deposit with no bacilli ever
A hypoxic, acidic, lipid-rich necrotic core that can harbour slowly replicating Mtb
check.answer: A hypoxic, acidic, lipid-rich necrotic core that can harbour slowly replicating Mtb
check.why: Latency is not sterility; caseum is one reason.

whyWrong.A sterile calcium deposit with no bacill: Calcification can follow; caseum is not proof of sterility.

check.prompt: INH is rapidly cidal against replicating bacilli making mycolate. In a closed hypoxic caseum with near-zero replication, INH’s expected contribution relative to a rifamycin is:
choices: Weaker sterilizing activity; INH’s strength is the replicating rim
Identical because MICs are measured in caseum
Zero because KatG is absent from Mtb
check.answer: Weaker sterilizing activity; INH’s strength is the replicating rim
check.why: Classical short-course logic: INH early cidal, rifamycin sterilizing, PZA lesion-pH.

whyWrong.Identical because MICs are measured in c: Broth MICs are not lesion PK.
